Here's an easier method: Simply put the chicken directly on a quarter sheet pan in the lower third of the oven, which provides more radiant heat to the thighs and legs. This cooks the underside properly just as the breast reaches temp, and - more importantly - creates a large surface area for fond that can be scraped for the sauce, finished with butter and a squeeze of fresh lemon. A little sauce improves and elevates almost every roasted poultry dish, bringing the entire plate together. Lastly, it's worth emphasizing just how important RESTING a roast chicken is, as this is the biggest mistake most home cooks make (besides not brining). If your chicken is steaming hot when carving and you have juice running onto the cutting board, you are not resting long enough. Wait 30 minutes, it will still be hot. If you don't have time to spare for dinner, just spatchcock the chicken, or - dare I say it - just buy a rotisserie chicken, which is usually better and cheaper.
